requirements.title: An accessible parent binding with the same local specific binding name is overridden
requirements.definition: A specific type-bound procedure specified in a type definition overrides a same-binding-name accessible type-bound procedure from the parent type, subject to the other binding and interface restrictions. Implementation procedure names need not match. An inaccessible private parent binding is inherited but is not overridden by a homonym in an unrelated module. The paragraph's parent wording is read with the binding taxonomy, generic-extension and name-collision rules: it is not permission to replace a generic or FINAL binding by a specific or to override a procedure-pointer component.

pending.binding-kind-boundary-source-use: PENDING — Source-use: 7.5.5 p4-p5/NOTE1, 7.5.7.2 p3 and 19.3.1 class(2) govern generic/specific collisions; 7.5.6 owns final bindings and R741/R742 own procedure-pointer components. Before any mixed-kind negative, isolate its actual canonical name/category cause and repair only that declaration. No local blanket 'same spelling always overrides' oracle.

requirements.oracle:
The exact planned observations are dynamic child22 versus parent component11, distinct names11/33, inaccessible identities7/9, and accessible private override22. Declarations establish binding identity; results test the selected implementation and do not themselves prove identity by equality. Shared premises P1-P7 in doc/fortran_2023_7_5_7_1.md apply. All read data and function results are defined, objects remain live, and the selected type/kind/rank/interface and accessibility conditions are established from original source, not processor representation.

Finite runtime implementation: 4 run-phase effect cases represent 5 facets using ordinary nonparameterized, nonabstract types. Primitive setup uses named components; every selected implementation verifies its defined receiver fields before returning an independent integer literal. Both dynamic and required explicit ancestor-view results are checked. All other facet plans remain pending. Separate content-bound source/case/evidence adjudications, not authorship or compiler outcomes, determine approval.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Use nonabstract parents for whole-parent-component calls; C911 forbids the tempting abstract-parent substitute. C789/C790 remain canonical DEFERRED/NON_OVERRIDABLE constraints. Private inheritance does not make an unrelated child module a descendant module.

requirements.title: Overriding interfaces either both have a passed object or both lack one
requirements.source: 7.5.7.3 p2, first bullet; PDF105, printed91, line6.
requirements.definition: The overriding and overridden interfaces both have a passed-object dummy argument, or neither does. Presence is semantic: default PASS counts just as bare PASS or PASS(name) does, whereas NOPASS suppresses the implicit object. This is distinct from existence or eligibility of a selected dummy under C784/C785/C765.

pending.pass-default-explicit-admission: PENDING — Compile admission/positive control: parent omits PASS/NOPASS and child uses PASS(self); each first dummy is named self, CLASS of its declaring type, scalar nonpointer nonallocatable IN. Both have a passed object and all other corresponding characteristics agree. No executed effect is inferred from acceptance.
pending.nopass-parity-admission: PENDING — Compile admission/positive control: both corresponding bindings use NOPASS and the same zero-dummy interface with concrete module targets. Both need NOPASS under C784; no receiver argument is invented.
pending.presence-mismatch-source-contrast: PENDING — Optional-policy/source contrast: parent explicitly PASS, child NOPASS, but both actual procedure interfaces deliberately have the identical CLASS(parent), IN dummy self. Child NOPASS therefore satisfies C784 and avoids a C765 child-type error. Repair only the parent's PASS to NOPASS, leaving both identical interfaces unchanged. Cause must be passed-object presence disagreement, not type or missing-dummy recovery.

requirements.title: Position-corresponding dummies preserve names and characteristics except passed-object type
requirements.source: 7.5.7.3 p2, seventh bullet; PDF105, printed91, lines12-13; characteristic definitions at PDF324.
requirements.definition: Dummy arguments corresponding by position have the same names and characteristics, except the type of passed-object dummies. The exception is not permission to alter the type of another dummy, kind or length properties, rank/shape, intent, optionality or pointer/allocatable status. Canonical 15.3.2 distinguishes data, procedure and asterisk dummies. Data characteristics include declared type/type parameters, shape unless assumed-rank, corank/codimensions, intent, OPTIONAL, ALLOCATABLE, ASYNCHRONOUS, CONTIGUOUS, VALUE, VOLATILE, polymorphism, POINTER and TARGET, plus exact dependence of nonconstant bounds/parameters and assumed/deferred properties. Dummy procedures retain interface explicitness, explicit procedure characteristics, POINTER and OPTIONAL. The comparison domain for newly added passed-object PDT parameters is separately unresolved; no blanket parameter waiver is asserted.

requirements.title: A public overridden binding cannot acquire a private override
requirements.source: 7.5.7.3 p2, ninth bullet; PDF105, printed91, line15.
requirements.definition: If the overridden binding is PUBLIC, the overriding binding is not PRIVATE. This is a one-way restriction on binding accessibility, not on the accessibility of the implementation procedure name or the type name. A PRIVATE parent binding that is accessible in the child's definition scope can be overridden with PRIVATE or PUBLIC, subject to the other conditions.

In an unrelated module the inaccessible private binding is not overridden at all; that different identity case remains S7.5.7.3-001's runtime plan.

requirements.title: Binding correspondence follows identity, overriding and inheritance
requirements.definition: A binding of a type corresponds to a binding of an extension when the latter is the same binding, overrides a corresponding binding, or inherits a corresponding binding.
